rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising whether braking is needed and whether the vehicle performs it. SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking behaviour itself as the subject of evaluation, while H-1 establishes the relevance of stopping in time to avoid collision. P remains focused on that behaviour and its operational context without incorporating sensing, computation, communication, or control mechanisms.
determining_elements: The vehicle’s 'braking-behaviour state' directly addresses performance or omission of the manoeuvre required by T.

Situations requiring braking to avoid collision are supported by H-1 and FR-7; the scope is not restricted to the single pedestrian scenario because these artefacts also address road users and static obstacles generally.
Whether braking occurs 'in time to avoid collision' concerns the temporal adequacy of braking itself, supported by H-1 and FR-7.1, rather than the timing of an observation mechanism.
The scope references obstacle-detection situations as operational context, not detection mechanisms or their failures as constituent parts of P.
